name: Thailand Privilege Visa (formerly Thailand Elite)
summary: Thailand Privilege (formerly Thailand Elite) is a paid membership run by a state-owned company. Membership comes with a long-term Privilege Entry visa of 5 to 20 years, depending on the tier, plus airport fast-track and concierge services. There is no income or asset test, just a background check and a one-off membership fee. It is a membership, not a work visa: you can't take a job in Thailand with it.
seoTitle: Thailand Privilege (Elite) Visa 2026: Tiers, Prices and Rules
seoDescription: Thailand Privilege membership visa explained: Gold, Platinum, Diamond and Reserve tiers and prices, stay per entry, extensions, family members, and why it's not a work visa.
validity: Depends on the tier: Gold 5 years, Platinum 10 years, Diamond 15 years, Reserve 20 years (Bronze, while it was offered, 5 years). The visa is multiple entry, and each entry gives you up to 1 year of stay.
extendableDetail: Each entry gives up to 1 year. If you stay longer without leaving, you extend for another year at your local immigration office, for 1,900 THB, as long as your membership is valid. Applications are accepted up to 30 days in advance, and you must attend in person for a photo and fingerprints.
feeNote: Membership fees, paid once: Gold 900,000 THB (5 years), Platinum 1,500,000 THB (10 years), Diamond 2,500,000 THB (15 years), Reserve 5,000,000 THB (20 years, by invitation only). The Bronze tier at 650,000 THB (5 years) is still shown on the official site, but applications are reported to close on 30 September 2026, which leaves Gold as the entry tier. Extensions of stay cost 1,900 THB each.
financialRequirement: No income, savings or asset test. What you need is enough money to pay the membership fee, which starts at 900,000 THB for the Gold tier.
processingTime: Most of the time goes on the background check by Thai authorities. Allow a few weeks to a few months between applying and receiving your membership approval, then book your visa appointment.
keyRequirements: Pay the membership fee for the chosen tier
Pass the background check: no serious criminal record, no history of overstaying or deportation from Thailand, not bankrupt
Family members need their own membership (Gold and below) or a 'Next Member' add-on on higher tiers
documents: Signed membership terms and consent for the background check
Proof of payment of the membership fee (after approval)
For extensions: passport with copies, 2 photos, TM7 extension form, TM30 receipt and your membership card
For family members: marriage or birth certificates

howToApply.detail: Compare the length of membership, the number of people covered and the yearly privilege points. Gold is the cheapest option from October 2026. Higher tiers allow family members to be added.

howToApply.step: Apply directly or through an authorised agent
howToApply.detail: Submit the application form and passport copy on thailandprivilege.co.th or through a General Sales and Service Agent (GSSA). Check that any agent is listed as authorised on the official site.
Thai authorities screen your record. If you're approved, you receive an approval letter and an invoice.
Pay the full fee as invoiced. Read the membership terms, including the refund and transfer rules, before you pay.
The visa is issued at a Thai embassy or consulate abroad or, if you're already in Thailand, at immigration. Your membership team books the appointment.

howToApply.step: Use your entries and extend when needed
howToApply.detail: Each entry gives up to 1 year. Extend at immigration if you stay longer, and keep up with 90-day reports; the membership service can help with these.

bestFor: Retirees and long-stay visitors who want to avoid proving income or holding a deposit
People who come and go often and want airport fast-track
Investors and business owners who want a long stay without dealing with yearly visa paperwork
Anyone who doesn't fit the age or income rules of other long-stay visas
notFor: Anyone who wants to work for a Thai company (you need a Non-B visa and work permit, or an LTR or SMART visa)
People on a budget: long-stay visas such as the DTV or retirement visas cost far less
Applicants with a criminal record or a Thai overstay history
Anyone who needs a work permit or a path to settle based on work or family
commonMistakes: Thinking the membership lets you work. It doesn't.
Forgetting that 90-day reports still apply if you stay 90 days in a row.
Paying unofficial agents or resellers extra fees. Buy directly or through an authorised agent.
Not checking which tier covers family members before buying separate memberships.
Overstaying past the 1-year stay on an entry without extending.

faqs.q: Is Thailand Privilege a visa or a membership?
faqs.a: It's a membership sold by Thailand Privilege Card Co., Ltd., a state-owned company. The membership comes with a long-term Privilege Entry visa and services such as airport fast-track. You're paying for the membership, and the visa is part of it.

faqs.q: Can I work in Thailand on a Thailand Privilege visa?
faqs.a: No. It is not a work visa and it doesn't let you get a work permit. To work for a Thai company you need a Non-B visa and work permit, or the LTR or SMART visa.

faqs.q: How long can I stay per entry?
faqs.a: Up to 1 year per entry. If you want to stay longer without leaving, extend for another year at immigration (1,900 THB) while your membership is valid.

The official site still lists Bronze at 650,000 THB for 5 years, but applications are reported to close on 30 September 2026. After that, Gold (900,000 THB, 5 years) is the cheapest tier. Check the official site for the current list.

faqs.q: Can I add my spouse or children?
faqs.a: Gold (and Bronze) cover one person, so each family member needs their own membership. Platinum, Diamond and Reserve allow family members to be added for a 'Next Member' fee. Thailand Privilege often runs a promotional price for this, so ask for the current offer.

faqs.q: Do I need to prove income or savings?
faqs.a: No. There's no financial test beyond paying the fee. You do have to pass a background check.

faqs.q: Do I still need to do 90-day reports?
faqs.a: Yes, if you stay in Thailand for 90 days in a row. Membership services can file these for you.
